metadata.title: Likelihood-Ranked Synthetic Selection in Self-Consuming Diffusion: An Imbalance-Dependent Boundary for Minority Retention
metadata.description:
Self-consuming training loops can induce model collapse. We study unlabeled likelihood ranking of synthetics in self-consuming DDPM training and report an imbalance-dependent boundary for minority retention—not a universal law. At ρ=5 (n=5), bottom>rand>top on all seeds; bootstrap 95% CIs for mean paired Δ vs random-k exclude zero. At ρ=7 the full order holds on 2/5 seeds; at ρ=10 (n=8) on 3/8. Strongest powered claim: top-k does not improve sliced W2 at generation 1 (18/18 cells; CI excludes zero).

Code: https://github.com/muhammadalamzeb/likelihood-rank-self-consuming-diffusion
metadata.notes: Empirical short preprint / workshop-scope note. Retention at rho=5 is directional (exact Wilcoxon floored at n=5); primary powered claim is W2 at generation 1. Stratified by imbalance rho.
